title: On-Prem Install Policy Friction — Digest and Tactical Actions (Mar 2027)
content:
Purpose:
Quick digest of policy friction observed across three recent on-prem installations (Mira Health, Qubex, and Argyle Labs). This is a tactical capture for the install team + solutions engineering -- not final runbook text. Contains observed blocker patterns, temporary mitigations, proposed runbook edits, and discrete action owners.

Attendees / who saw/edited this note:
- Miguel Alvarez (owner) -- install lead
- Priya Shah -- net/infra SME, oncall for Mira Health install
- Ethan O'Connor -- solutions eng (customer liaison)
- Rhea Banerjee -- security & compliance advisor
- Samir Gupta -- field engineer (Qubex install)

Summary (TL;DR):
- Three installs this sprint surfaced a common theme: org/legal/policy constraints on inbound management ports and customer lock-down of internal DNS that breaks our node discovery.
- Primary customer blockers: 1) Outbound allowlist for telemetry/control plane (requires SOC signoff), 2) Internal DNS split-horizon causing cert hostname mismatches during service boot, 3) Corporate proxy that rewrites TLS SNI (breaks mTLS verification).
- Short term: patch the bootstrap flow to support manual seed IP entry + CA bundle upload, and add a proxy-aware TLS handshake mode.
- Long term: update runbook + installer UI to expose these knobs and add a compliance checklist step with templated customer L3 contacts.

Detailed observations by customer:
1) Mira Health (large hospital chain) -- installer failed at node discovery (kafka/consul-like discovery). Root cause: customer uses internal DNS namespace that returns 127.0.0.1 for certain hostnames that conflict with our expected service FQNs. Also, security team denies outbound to telemetry.redwood.ai until SOC review completes.
   - Impact: installation paused Day 1 -> 3, on-site SE escalated to SOC.
   - Temporary mitigation performed: we switched to manual static peers file, uploaded CA cert, and disabled auto-telemetry (local logging only).

2) Qubex (mid-market SaaS) -- corporate proxy rewrites SNI and injects headers causing mutual TLS to fail between the node and control plane; intermittent certificate validation errors during rolling restart.
   - Impact: cluster enters degraded state during scaleout.
   - Mitigation: field engineer applied a TLS fallback allowing plaintext control traffic over a private management VLAN (customer approved for timeboxed window).

3) Argyle Labs (finance customer) -- strict egress allowlist + IDS that rejects unknown certificates. They requested us to bring the management plane endpoints into their allowlist but required SOC package (summary of endpoints, certificates, hashes). The SOC pack we provided was incomplete (missed ephemeral endpoints used for agent staging).
   - Impact: multi-day handoff with legal + procurement.
   - Mitigation: provided enhanced SOC bundle and a checklist for procurement teams (work in progress).

Common root causes (pattern analysis):
- Installer assumes DNS and egress will be mostly permissive. Real customers are lock-down by default.
- No built-in manual bootstrap path in the UI for customers that want zero DNS reliance.
- Telemetry and control plane endpoints are not sufficiently stable/observable in the SOC bundle (we leak ephemeral staging endpoints).
- Lack of a standard proxy/TLS compatibility mode documented for on-prem installs.

Proposed immediate changes (next 2 sprints) -- tactical: (owners + due dates)
- Add "Manual Bootstrap" mode to installer: allow paste of seed node IPs + upload of CA bundle (Owner: Samir Gupta, due: 2027-03-30).
- Create a proxy-aware TLS handshake option (non-default) that disables SNI checks for environments with corporate TLS rewrite (Owner: Priya Shah, due: 2027-04-06).
- Produce a "SOC Pack v2" that enumerates long-lived + ephemeral endpoints, cert fingerprints, and a sample security questionnaire (Owner: Rhea Banerjee, due: 2027-03-22).
- Update the install checklist template to require named L3 contact and procurement SLA (Owner: Ethan O'Connor, due: 2027-03-25).

Proposed mid-term changes (next quarter) -- strategic:
- Installer UI: add preflight network test that simulates DNS resolution, outbound allowlist, and proxy behavior. Fail with clear remediation steps.
- Runbook: canonical flow for "no outbound" customers: local-only install mode + manual telemetry export (SFTP/USB).
- Security: automation to generate SOC packages per customer region and provide signed ephemeral certs for bootstrap to avoid exposing staging endpoints.

Open action items / blockers table (short):
- PS-1: Samir to implement opt-in manual bootstrap UI flag + backend handler (in progress).
- PS-2: Priya to prototype TLS SNI bypass in staging and demo with Qubex (needs security signoff).
- PS-3: Rhea to compile SOC-pack v2 and circulate to solutions eng for validation (blocked on list of ephemeral endpoints from infra).
- PS-4: Ethan to update handoff email template used by SEs when booking SOC review call.

Notes from today's standup (freeform):
- Miguel: "we need to stop treating DNS as assumed; add checkboxes and tests up front. Also -- ask legal for a one-pager we can hand to customers for procurement."
- Priya: "proxy case is uglier than expected -- some customers use TLS inspection boxes that rewrite the cert SAN. We can either accept a bypass or push customers to allow management VLANs."
- Rhea: "SOC packs historically come late. I'll own a small generator script that pulls current endpoint set from infra and outputs a zip. This will take ~3 days."
- Samir: "Manual bootstrap already saved the Mira Health day; let's make the UX simple (paste list, confirm certs)."

Risks / heatmap (quick):
- High: Customer legal/procurement timelines (mitigation: set expectations and provide templated docs).
- Medium: Complexity of TLS probe compatibility across multiple proxy vendors (mitigation: test matrix + preferred configuration list).
- Low: Installer UI bloat -- we must keep default path simple.

Draft language for runbook additions (copy/paste friendly):
- "If DNS returns unexpected IPs or service FQNs do not resolve to private network addresses, switch to Manual Bootstrap mode: collect seed IPs from customer, upload their CA bundle, and start cluster in disconnected mode. Document the IP mapping in the install ticket."
- "Proxy/TLS mode: if customer uses TLS inspection that alters SNI, enable 'proxy-compatible TLS' in advanced settings and work with security to validate the handshake logs. This should be used for short windows and only after risk approval."

Customer communication snippets (for SE to send):
- "To avoid install delays, please provide: 1) named L3 contact for network and SOC, 2) allowlist entries for the management endpoints in the attached SOC pack, 3) confirmation on whether the environment uses TLS inspection/proxy boxes. If you cannot provide outbound allowlist, we can proceed with 'local-only' install -- see options."

Follow-ups and next syncs:
- Install triage on 2027-03-18 (09:30 PT) -- demo of manual bootstrap flow + review of SOC Pack v2.
- Field Q&A with Qubex scheduled 2027-03-20 (14:00 PT) to validate TLS bypass approach.
- Deliverables check on 2027-03-22 (Rhea to confirm SOC pack).

Notes to self (unfinished ideas):
- Consider shipping a small hardened usb image with the CA + bootstrap script for very locked environments (airgap adjacent).
- Long term: a 'management tunnel' appliance we ship that terminates TLS inside customer network and exposes a local control plane (hardware + support cost tradeoffs).

Appendix (logs / quick references):
- Example error lines seen at Qubex: "mTLS handshake failed: unexpected certificate subject; SNI mismatch to 10.0.3.21"
- Mira Health ticket: JIRA-PS-4821 (networking) -- internal notes attached.
- Quick links: Confluence runbook draft (see linked_artifacts).

If you have edits, add them inline or ping me in slack (#p-deploy). This will be reshaped into a runbook patch once the demos validate the TLS fallback approach.
